_meta.project: JointCheck — workmanship grading with a deterministic rule lookup
_meta.status: SEED — thresholds are PROVISIONAL and MUST be calibrated in ticket B-T24
integrity_warnings: IPC-A-610 and J-STD-001 are TRADEMARKED standards owned by IPC / IPC-WHMA. Their text and official accept/reject photographs are paid material.
DO NOT reproduce substantial verbatim text from them. DO NOT use their official photographs. DO NOT imply endorsement or certification.

DO NOT invent clause numbers. Every rule_id here is our own (JC-*). A rule may only carry an external clause reference if a human with legal access to the standard has verified it, and then verified_against_primary_source must be true with their name and the edition.

The class_thresholds below are PROVISIONAL PLACEHOLDERS set to plausible round numbers so the pipeline can be built. They are NOT sourced values. Ticket B-T24 calibrates each one against the double-labelled test set and records before/after in docs/DECISIONS.md.
Any rule with human_reviewed=false is EXCLUDED from the gate when STRICT_MODE is on, and its exclusion is recorded. Do not ship a gate built on unreviewed numbers without saying so.

The required public statement, verbatim, in README + artifact footer + video + Devpost copy: 'An independent tool aligned to publicly documented electronics workmanship criteria. Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified against IPC-A-610 or J-STD-001. Thresholds are ours, calibrated on our own labelled test set.'

class_definitions.1: General electronic products — consumer/low-cost items where the primary requirement is that the assembly functions. Cosmetic imperfections are broadly tolerated.
class_definitions.2: Dedicated service electronic products — where continued performance and extended life are required, and for which uninterrupt service is desirable but not critical. Cosmetic defects may be allowed.
class_definitions.3: High-reliability electronic products — where continued high performance or performance-on-demand is critical, equipment downtime cannot be tolerated, end-use environment may be exceptionally harsh, and the equipment must function when required (medical, life support, aerospace, military).
class_definitions.source_note: These three class descriptions are widely reproduced in public electronics-assembly training material and vendor documentation. Confirm the exact wording against an openly licensed source and record it in docs/STANDARDS-POSITION.md before publishing them to users. Do NOT present them as a quotation from the standard unless you have verified that they are.

verdict_definitions.ACCEPT: Meets the criterion for the selected class.
verdict_definitions.PROCESS_INDICATOR: Not a defect at this class, but a condition that signals a process problem worth correcting. Including this middle grade is deliberate: a binary pass/fail tool reads as naive to anyone who has worked in production.
verdict_definitions.REJECT: Fails the criterion for the selected class.
verdict_definitions.UNDETERMINED: Cannot be decided. The gate abstains and routes to a human inspector with a reason code and a fix instruction.

image_quality_floors.note: Calibrate blur_laplacian_var_min empirically in B-T05: it must separate the 10 deliberately-bad test images from the good ones with ZERO overlap. Record the two distributions in docs/EVAL.md. 60 is a starting guess, not a sourced value.

confidence_floors.note: A condition with measurement_basis='visual_only' and confidence below the floor becomes UNDETERMINED, never a verdict.

rules.title: Solder must wet the pad and the lead, forming a concave fillet with visible flow
rules.plain_english: The solder has to actually spread onto the metal, not just sit on it as a bead. A dull, rounded blob that pulls away from the pad is a cold or non-wetted joint.

secondary_verdict.when: coverage is within 10 points of the class threshold and the surface is dull
secondary_verdict.note: borderline wetting usually indicates a temperature or fluxing process problem

source.reference: Provisional threshold. To be calibrated in B-T24 against the double-labelled test set at a Class-3 precision floor of 0.90.

rules.threshold_provenance: PROVISIONAL — set by us as a plausible starting value. Not a sourced number.

rules.title: The joint must contain enough solder to form a continuous fillet between lead and land
rules.plain_english: Not enough solder. The fillet is thin or missing over part of the joint, so the mechanical and electrical connection is weak.

rules.title: Excess solder that obscures the joint outline, or that forms a convex blob, is not acceptable at higher classes
rules.plain_english: Too much solder. You should still be able to see the shape of the joint underneath. A shiny ball that hides the lead is a classic over-application.

secondary_verdict.when: joint outline not visible but no bridging or clearance risk
secondary_verdict.note: excess solder is more often a process signal than a reliability defect at Class 1–2

rules.title: No solder may connect two electrically separate conductors
rules.plain_english: Solder has bridged across to a neighbouring pad or pin. This is a short circuit.
rules.class_sensitivity_note: Bridge detection is largely class-INDEPENDENT — a short is a short. The Class-3 minimum clearance of 0.10 mm is a provisional margin, not a sourced value. This is worth saying on camera: some criteria are class-sensitive and some are not, and knowing which is which is the domain knowledge.

rules.title: Icicles (solder spikes projecting from the joint) are limited by length and by clearance risk
rules.plain_english: A sharp spike of solder sticking out. It can break off, become debris, or short against something nearby.

rules.title: Detached solder balls/splash must be removed; size and proximity to conductors decide the class verdict
rules.plain_english: Loose blobs of solder left on the board. They can move and cause a short later.

secondary_verdict.when: ball is within the size limit but lies within 0.5 mm of an exposed conductor

rules.threshold_provenance: PROVISIONAL — set by us. Class 3 = zero tolerance is a deliberate conservative choice, not a sourced value.

rules.title: A two-terminal chip component must sit flat on both terminations; lifted-end angle decides the verdict
rules.plain_english: One end of the component has stood up like a tombstone. That end is not soldered at all.
rules.measurement_caveat: tombstone_lift_deg requires the component body contour to be visible against the board. When it is not, S3 MUST return value=null with reason 'component_contour_not_resolvable' and the gate MUST abstain with 'measurement_not_computable'. Never estimate an angle from a single 2D view without the body contour — that is exactly the 'hallucination with a decimal point' failure this project exists to avoid.

rules.title: Solder and wire strands must maintain clearance from the board surface and from adjacent conductors
rules.plain_english: Solder or a stray wire strand is too close to the board or to the next pad. It can arc or short.

rules.title: Stranded wire must not have severed, splayed or folded strands at the termination
rules.plain_english: Some of the little copper wires inside the cable are cut, bent back, or sticking out. The joint is weaker than it looks.
rules.measurement_caveat: Counting severed strands from a single photo is often not possible. Prefer the visual_only path with an explicit confidence, and abstain below the floor.

rules.title: Flux residue must not exceed a class-dependent fraction of the local area, and must not bridge conductors
rules.plain_english: Leftover flux gunk. Some is normal; a lot of it traps moisture and can be corrosive or conductive.

secondary_verdict.when: within limit but visibly bridging two conductors

rules.measurement_caveat: Flux residue detection is colour-space dependent and highly sensitive to white balance and no-clean vs rosin flux type. Record the flux type when known. If unknown, widen the abstention band and say so.

rules.title: Void fraction in the solder mass must not exceed a class-dependent limit
rules.plain_english: Air bubbles trapped inside the solder. Too many weaken the joint and trap heat.
rules.measurement_caveat: For BGA, voiding is normally assessed by X-ray, NOT by optical inspection. An optical void_fraction for a BGA is almost certainly invalid — the gate MUST abstain with 'measurement_not_computable' for joint_type='bga' unless the user supplies an X-ray image, in which case record the modality. Getting this right is itself an insider signal.

rules.title: A joint disturbed during solidification shows a frosted/granular surface and must be reflowed or replaced
rules.plain_english: The joint moved while the solder was cooling, so it has a grainy, frosted look instead of being smooth and shiny. It looks soldered but it is weak.
rules.class_sensitivity_note: Deliberately class-INDEPENDENT: a disturbed joint is not acceptable at any class. Another example of knowing which criteria are class-sensitive and which are not.

source.reference: TODO_VERIFY — locate an openly licensed description of disturbed/disturbed-solder joints and record the URL + retrieval date, or set kind='own_validated_measurement'

rules.threshold_provenance: Visual-only; no numeric threshold. Confidence floor is ours.

rules.title: The component body must be free of cracks, chips and thermal damage; terminations must be intact
rules.plain_english: The part itself is cracked or chipped, or its metal ends are damaged. Nothing about the solder can save it.

source.reference: TODO_VERIFY — record an openly licensed source, or use kind='own_validated_measurement'

rules.title: The copper land must remain bonded to the substrate; any lifting is a reject regardless of class
rules.plain_english: The copper pad has peeled up off the board. The joint is hanging on by nothing.

rules.title: Where a component is polarity-sensitive, the marking orientation must match the board marking
rules.plain_english: The part is in backwards. Diodes, electrolytic capacitors, ICs and connectors all have a direction.
rules.applicability_precondition: Only applies when BOTH a component polarity marking AND a board polarity marking are visible. If either is not visible, abstain — do not guess.
rules.threshold_provenance: Visual-only. The precondition (both markings visible) is the important part.

disclaimer.short: JointCheck is an independent screening tool aligned to publicly documented electronics workmanship criteria. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified against IPC-A-610 or J-STD-001. Thresholds are ours, calibrated on our own labelled test set. It is not a certified inspection system and must not be the sole acceptance authority for a product.
